scientific_integrity: The sharp global comparison constant \(C_*\), its one-uniform extremizer, and the threshold \(t_0\) are treated as prior. The claimed contribution is only the exact local reduction of the optimized ratio to the dominant coefficient and the resulting quadratic coefficient-space deficit. The proof is analytic; numerical calculations only replay constants and finite-sum stress cases. Search failure is not treated as proof of historical novelty, and residual overlap risk from older cube-slab or weighted-uniform literature is disclosed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is local near one-sparse coefficient vectors in residual \(\ell_1\) distance. It does not provide a global deficit bound for arbitrary weights, does not settle intermediate-dimensional extremizers, and does not optimize the radius of the local neighborhood.
title: Quadratic stability of the sharp Gaussian tail constant near one-sparse uniform sums
